findings.note: AGENTS.md's ui-shot non-negotiable and the finding's own verification_plan step 3 ('pnpm ui-shot against the Patch view to confirm no mirror control is visible today') were NOT run — verification.commands lists only pnpm typecheck / pnpm gates / pnpm design-system. In practice the omission is vacuous: PatchMirrorControl has had no importer since 39b7d6b, independently re-verified here (rg for 'PatchMirrorControl' across the repo returns zero hits outside docs/plans and the pre-fix design-system bundle), so no rendered surface can change and the deadness rests on the import graph — which fix.schema.json's own parity_check note accepts as the correct evidence for a 0%-coverage region. Recorded because the evidence chain that landed is weaker than the one the finding specified, not because the conclusion is in doubt.

Record inaccuracy in 05-fixes/batch-02.json notes: it says THREE tests were retargeted off `mirror` onto surviving fields, but FOUR were. The unlisted fourth is store.routing.test.ts:96 'carries hoopCount + defaultHoopSpacingMm and leaves mirror untouched' -> '...leaves the other globals untouched', whose unrelated-field-preserved assertion moved from a hardcoded `expect(kit.global.mirror).toBe('none')` literal onto a captured-before `maxPixelsPerOutput` value. All four retargets were read line by line: assertion COUNT and SHAPE are unchanged in every one ('undoes a kit-global edit' and 'interleaves cleanly' are structural clones of the mirror originals with expanded substituted; 'emits every changed slice at once (mixed edit)' still asserts kinds toEqual ['setKitGlobal','setOutput']), so no assertion was weakened — only the batch record undercounts. Note the `expanded` substitution arguably strengthens two of them, since expanded also drives reconcileOutputs whereas mirror did not.

Predicted-vs-actual interface drift, recorded for the audit trail only: the finding's interface_delta predicted 1 exported symbol removed, interface_delta_actual is 2 (store.setKitMirror plus the PatchMirrorControl default export). This is EXPECTED and approved — Trent's 2026-07-29 decision took the finding's option (b) and expanded the scope end-to-end. Independently confirmed that reflectWorld was module-private in pixel-model.ts, so the count of 2 is exact. Separately, the finding's own evidence block contains a factual ERROR that the implementer correctly caught and refused to act on: it claims 'No apps/web caller survives' for setKitGlobal. Verified false — PatchKitInspector.svelte:33/43/53/63, PatchControllerInspector.svelte:160 and shot-seam.ts:442 all call store.setKitGlobal today. Blindly executing option (b) as literally written would have removed a live C1/C2 kit-config path. The narrowing to the `mirror` FIELD only is the correct call.

parity_check.reason: Counted from the diff, not trusted from the report: `git diff 5423e09 a7c46eb -- '*.test.ts'` yields 15 removed `it(`/`test(` lines and 2 added, net -13, which is exactly 2981 - 2968. The 2 added lines are renames of retargeted survivors ('carries hoopCount + defaultHoopSpacingMm and leaves the other globals untouched', 'undoes a kit-global edit'), so 13 test cases were genuinely deleted: mirror.test.ts 7 (whole file), kit-global-forwarding.test.ts 3, project-resync.test.ts 2, store.routing.test.ts 1. Every deleted title is mirror-only. No it.each / it.skip / it.only anywhere in the diff, so no case multiplies. Coverage loss from the 2 deleted project-resync tests is nil: they asserted the setKitGlobal partial stays minimal across two fields, and with mirror gone globalPartial has a single field (`expanded`), making minimality degenerate; the surviving 'carries expanded on setKitGlobal, emitted BEFORE setKitOutputs' still pins the ordering invariant those tests shared.
